audit.whatIsWrong: Kayle's attack range is attributed to her E in three places: mid ("her ranged E and waveclear appear"), whys[4] ("Kayle's level-6 ranged E"), spikes[1] ("E ranged and waveclear come online").
audit.why: Divine Ascent (P) is what grants range: "Kayle's attacks are empowered by the heavens as she levels up and spends skill points... she progressively gains Attack Speed, Move Speed, Attack Range, and waves of fire on her attacks." Her E is Starfire Spellblade, an on-next-attack effect at 550 range. A Zac player watching her E for the range step is watching the wrong ability, and will misjudge when she can no longer be walked down.
audit.corrected: The range comes from Divine Ascent (P) as she levels; her E is Starfire Spellblade.

audit.whatIsWrong: Starfire Spellblade's missing-health scaling is nowhere in the entry, and neither is the fact that Zac pays for his own abilities in health.
audit.why: Riot's text: Starfire Spellblade "smites her target with celestial fire, dealing bonus damage proportionate to their missing health." Zac's Q, W and E all list costType "% of current Health". So Zac lowers his own health to cast, and every point he spends makes her E hit harder — a feedback loop that no other tank matchup has in quite this form, and one that argues for picking blobs back up before she is in range rather than after.
audit.corrected: Starfire Spellblade scales with your missing health, and your Q, W and E all cost current health.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this entry for having no cooldown sequencing anywhere, and both layers say only "Track Divine Judgment before every commit" / "Bait it".
audit.why: Divine Judgment is 160s at rank 1. That is not a cooldown you trade around, it is a cooldown you spend a lane exploiting — bait it once and Zac has roughly two full minutes of unanswered engage. Radiant Blast at 12s and Celestial Blessing at a flat 15s are the numbers that actually govern minute-to-minute trades.
audit.corrected: Divine Judgment 160s at rank 1; Radiant Blast 12s; Celestial Blessing a flat 15s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Radiant Blast is never mentioned, and neither is its resistance reduction.
audit.why: Riot's text: Radiant Blast summons a sword "that pierces through enemies, slowing, damaging, and reducing the resistances of all hit", at 900 range on 12s at rank 1. Against a Zac building resistances every recall, a 900-range shred on a 12-second cooldown is both the reason to respect her poke and the specific window to walk up in once it is spent.
audit.corrected: Radiant Blast is 12s at rank 1, reaches 900, and reduces resistances — walk up on its cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appears once in the full layer's breakdown.late boilerplate and nowhere in the content layer.
audit.why: Celestial Blessing heals her and grants Move Speed on a flat 15s cooldown, and it is her only sustain. In the early lane that makes it the thing to trade around; in the late game, where she is the 9.5/10 carry this entry describes, Grievous Wounds is what stops it compounding. _missing-interactions.json flags this matchup for needs-antiheal on exactly that ability.
audit.corrected: Celestial Blessing is her only heal, flat 15s — trade around it early, buy Grievous Wounds late.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] calls level 6 "a soft point" whose content is "E ranged and waveclear", with no mention of Divine Judgment arriving at the same time.
audit.why: Level 6 gives her both the first Divine Ascent range step and her ultimate. Calling it soft while omitting the ultimate is the wrong shape: it is a real spike, but a spike with a 160-second recharge, which is exactly what makes baiting it worth planning around.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is her passive range step plus Divine Judgment — a real spike, on a 160s recharge.
